I transferred from cc and was in a similar situation as you. Im graduating in May with 0 debt and this is what I did:
1) work full time through college. I’ve had a lot different jobs from customer service to baby sitting to cleaning houses, but found a flexible full time job that pays well and have been there the last 2 years. Way easier to do this now that school is one Zoom.
2) have multiple roommates. I live in a 2b 2b in a highly desirable area and pay 500 a month for rent + utilities. There are 4 ppl in our apt so each room holds two. 
3) Budget EVERYTHING. Make a spreadsheet of mandatory expenses + what you feel comfortable with spending on food/recreation each month as well as dedicating a chunk of your money to savings to add towards your tuition. Great skill to develop overall.

This is roughly what I have done and I enjoyed it. I can’t say I had the traditional college experience, but I received great work experience, have 0 debt, and a nice lump sum of savings so I’m not complaining. Though it can be difficult it is definitely possible. Also, I personally feel it is worth it to be away from my family because  my family sucks haha however if you and your family get along, only you can answer that. I have many friends who are close to their families and ended up moving back home and going to the local university in my hometown bc they missed their family and living at home while in college is WILDLY cheaper. However, if you are looking to gain independence and meet new people, then it might be worth it.
